decision_reason: isolated role projection, permission metadata and source guards independently show that a read action is accepted as Mapping create/update/delete authority, directly violating R8

causal_assessment.hypothesis: MappingController and MappingsPage copied broad legacy data-migration:manage/write fallbacks instead of using the approved mapping action permissions
supporting_evidence: DATA_MIGRATION_DEVELOPER has mappings read but no mappings:create/update/delete
data-migration:manage has action_code read and is assigned to DATA_MIGRATION_DEVELOPER
Mapping write guards explicitly accept data-migration:manage
causal_assessment.falsifier: a runtime POST/PUT/DELETE request from DATA_MIGRATION_DEVELOPER returns 403 and the page hides write controls without changing the guards

control_action.target: Mapping-specific write permission expressions and matching frontend visibility
invariants: view and download remain available to the Mapping read permission
DATA_MIGRATION_ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN retain mapping write ability through granular permissions or system authority
service-level owner/admin, project and attachment authorization remains unchanged
no public permission implementation or other content menu is modified
control_action.impact_limit: three Mapping-specific files and direct regression checks
control_action.rollback: restore only the three Mapping-specific permission expressions/tests
correction_check: MappingControllerSecurityTest rejects data-migration:manage and data-migration:write in write annotations
mobile Mapping page hides create and manage actions while retaining download

residual_risk: other data-migration menus continue to use legacy fallbacks and are outside this Mapping-specific requirement scope
